A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MotionStream work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original motion-transfer and camera-control evaluations, ablations, and a 2,800-response user study in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds the motion-conditioning comparison in Table A4.

M1.justification: The track head, joint guidance, Self Forcing/DMD, attention sinks, rolling KV cache, and Tiny VAE are retained. V2's explicit teacher-score equation clarifies the procedure already described in v1 Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Table A4 extends the Sora evaluation to generation with all motion inputs withheld, using only image and text conditioning. The datasets remain unchanged; the world-exploration scenario illustrated in v2 was already discussed in v1 Appendix F.

E2.justification: Table A4 adds Wan 2.1 14B I2V as a directly evaluated baseline. Its previous use as a backbone or synthetic-data generator did not constitute this comparison. Existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added Table A4 experiment compares the 1.3B teacher and student with motion conditioning present versus absent, includes a 14B I2V reference, and introduces FVD alongside existing VBench metrics. Previously reported evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a targeted analysis of generative quality with and without motion conditioning. Figure A6 adds a concrete world-exploration failure example supporting an existing limitation. Earlier guidance, attention, chunk-size, and VAE ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains its latency and throughput variability reporting. Table A4 supplies point estimates without introducing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table A4 adds baseline and motion-absent scores plus FVD: teacher 578.2/1550.4 and student 745.8/1532.5 with/without motion, versus 1274.6 for Wan 2.1 14B I2V. These are newly reported comparisons; Tables 1–4 and A1–A3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2's Equation 4 and explicit critic formula restate the jointly guided teacher and unguided critic already specified in v1 Section 3.2. The underlying mathematics is unchanged, with no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The new introduction contribution list explicitly claims first-time systematic exploration of attention sinks and local attention with extrapolation-aware training. The abstract and conclusion retain their existing performance and application claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets the results as preserving generative quality and counteracting I2V static bias, and hypothesizes that text-dominated CFG causes teacher instability without motion. The scene-transition limitation illustrated in Figure A6 was already stated in v1.

D1.justification: Training, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, timing, and evaluation instructions in Appendices A, D, and E are retained, as are access and reproducibility statements. The expanded score exposition clarifies existing documentation without disclosing new implementation settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds Choi et al. (2025), on adaptive low-pass guidance, to support its discussion of I2V static bias and makes novelty positioning more explicit in the contribution list. Section 2 and the existing comparisons with prior distillation methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds a four-point contribution list, expands the Section 3 overview and teacher/critic guidance explanation, and corrects author-name spelling and minor wording. The overall section order and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table A4, expands Figure A6 with a five-frame world-exploration row, and revises Figure 2's caption. Existing figures and tables are retained with limited repositioning and text reflow.

improvement.justification: Table A4 provides useful evidence about removing motion conditioning, Figure A6 illustrates an existing failure boundary, and the distillation explanation is clearer. These modest gains leave the core method and benchmarks unchanged. The new comparison uses a 14B baseline against 1.3B models and reports no uncertainty, limiting its support for preservation of the base model's generative quality.
